questions.question: What is the mean of the numbers 3, 5, 7, 5, 5?
questions.explain: Add all five numbers (25) and divide by 5 to get 5. A common trap is to count the digits instead of the data values, or to pick a value that 'looks in the middle' without dividing.

questions.question: What is the median of the numbers 12, 4, 8, 2, 10?
questions.explain: Sort first: 2, 4, 8, 10, 12. The middle (3rd) value is 8. The most common mistake is picking a value without sorting, or confusing the median with the mean (7.2).

questions.question: What is the mode of the numbers 2, 4, 4, 6, 3, 4, 1?
questions.explain: Count how many times each number appears. The number 4 shows up three times, more than any other, so it is the mode. A trap is to pick the middle value or the largest value instead of the most frequent one.

questions.question: A student's five quiz scores are 70, 80, 90, 80, 80. What is the mode?
questions.explain: The score 80 appears three times, while 70 and 90 each appear only once, so 80 is the mode. Don't pick the highest score or a number like 85 that is not even in the data.

questions.question: Emma collected cans of food for her school's winter drive over five days: 5, 3, 7, 6, and 9 cans. What is the mean number of cans per day?
questions.explain: Add the five values (30) and divide by 5 to get a mean of 6 cans per day. The median here is also 6, but there is no mode, so be sure you are actually dividing the sum by the count.

questions.question: The prices of five pairs of sneakers at a BC store are $45, $62, $38, $55, and $70. What is the median price?
questions.explain: Sort the prices: $38, $45, $55, $62, $70. The 3rd value is $55. A common error is to average the two middle values (that is only needed with an even count) or to report the mean of $54 instead.

questions.question: Liam's goals in six soccer games were 1, 3, 0, 2, 3, 1. Which statement about the mode is correct?
options: The mode is 2 because it is the middle value.
The mode is 1 and 3 because both appear exactly twice.
The mode is 0 because it is the smallest value.
There is no mode because no single number appears more than any other.
questions.explain: Both 1 and 3 appear twice, so the data set is bimodal. A frequent mistake is to declare 'no mode' whenever two values tie, or to confuse the mode with the median.

questions.question: A class of 11 students has reading scores: 55, 62, 68, 71, 74, 77, 79, 82, 85, 90, 96. A new student joins and scores 50. What happens to the median?
options: It increases because a new data point was added.
It stays at 77 because 50 is below the original median.
It becomes 74 because the data set now has an even number of values.
questions.explain: With 12 values the median is the average of the 6th and 7th: (74 + 77)/2 = 75.5. Students often forget that an even count changes how you find the median, or assume adding a low value cannot lower it.

questions.question: A Vancouver bakery sold 10, 12, 11, 50, 13, 11, and 9 cupcakes over seven days (the 50 was a one-time school order). The owner wants to describe a 'typical' day. Which measure of central tendency is most appropriate, and why?
options: The mean of about 17, because it uses every data point in the calculation.
The median of 11, because the outlier of 50 pulls the mean too high to be typical.
The mode of 11, because it is the single most frequent value.
All three are equally valid because the data is roughly symmetric.
questions.explain: The outlier 50 makes the mean (about 16.6) unrepresentative of an ordinary day, while the median and mode both sit at 11. The key skill is recognising that an extreme value distorts the mean but leaves the median stable.

questions.question: The mean of four numbers is 20. A fifth number is added and the new mean becomes 24. What is the fifth number?
questions.explain: Four numbers sum to 80 (4 × 20); five numbers sum to 120 (5 × 24). The added number is 120 − 80 = 40. The trap is to subtract the two means (24 − 20 = 4) or to answer with the new mean itself.

questions.question: A teacher says, 'The median is always the middle number in the list.' Which data set shows the teacher is WRONG?
questions.explain: With an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values: (4 + 6)/2 = 5, a number not in the data set. Students often assume the median must always be an actual value from the list.

questions.question: The mean of five numbers is 30. The largest number is removed, and the mean of the remaining four is 25. What was the largest number?
questions.explain: The original sum is 5 × 30 = 150; the new sum is 4 × 25 = 100. The removed (largest) number is 150 − 100 = 50. A common error is to subtract the two means (30 − 25 = 5) instead of working with the total sums.
